text: κέλευσμα, a word of command, a call.
gloss: a word of command, a call

text: κενοδοξία (cenodoxia), vainglory.
κενόδοξος, vainglorious.
κενοφωνία, a worthless utterance.
κενόω, (a) I empty, Phil. ii 7; (b) I deprive of content; make unreal.
κέντρον, a goad.
κεντυρίων (Lat., = Gk. ἑκατοντάρχης), a centurion, an officer commanding about a hundred infantry in the Roman army.
Κενχρεαί, Cenchreae, the harbour town of Corinth on the Saronic Gulf.
gloss: Cenchreae, the harbour town of Corinth on the Saronic Gulf

text: κενῶς, falsely.
κεραία (variation κερέα), a little hook, an apostrophe on letters of the alphabet, distinguishing them from other like letters, or a separation stroke between letters.
gloss: a little hook, an apostrophe on letters of the alphabet

text: κεραμεύς, a potter.
κεραμικός, of clay, made by a potter.
gloss: of clay, made by a potter

text: κεράμιον, an earthenware pitcher.
κέραμος, a tile; οἱ κέραμοι, practically the roof.
κεράννυμι, I mix.
κεράτιον, a husk (pod) of the carob (siliqua graeca).
κέρδος, gain.
κέρμα, a small coin: plur. small change.
κερματιστής, properly a changer of large into smaller coins, a money-changer.
gloss: a changer of large into smaller coins, a money-changer

text: κεφάλαιον, (a) the chief matter, the main point, Heb. viii 1; (b) a sum of money, Ac. xxii 28.
gloss: the chief matter, the main point

text: κεφαλιόω, I wound in the head.
κεφαλίς, (lit. little head, then the knob at the end of the wooden core of a roll of papyrus, then) a roll.
κημόω (from κῆμος, a muzzle), I muzzle.
κῆνσος (Latin census), poll-tax.
κῆπος, a garden.
κηπουρός, keeper of a garden.
κήρυγμα, a proclamation.
κῆρυξ, a herald, proclaimer.
κῆτος, a sea monster, a huge sea fish.
gloss: a sea monster, a huge sea fish

text: Κηφᾶς, Cephas (Aram. for rock), the new name given to Simon, the disciple.
gloss: Cephas, the new name given to Simon, the disciple

text: κιβωτός, (properly a wooden box, hence) the Ark, in which Noah sailed.
gloss: the Ark, in which Noah sailed

text: κιθάρα, a harp.
κιθαρίζω, intr. and tr., I play on the harp, I harp, with acc. of the tune.
gloss: I play on the harp, I harp

text: κιθαρῳδός, a harpist.
Κιλικία, Cilicia, a Roman province between the Taurus range of mountains and the coast in the SE. corner of Asia Minor, linked up with the province of Syria.
κινδυνεύω, I am in danger, sometimes c. infin. of . . .
κίνδυνος, danger, peril, risk.
κινέω, tr. I move; I stir, excite.
κιννάμωμον (a Semitic word), cinnamon.
κλάσις, breaking.
κλάσμα, a fragment.
Κλαυδία, Claudia, a Christian woman in Rome; if historical, probably a freedwoman of the imperial household.
gloss: Claudia, a Christian woman in Rome

text: Κλαύδιος, (a) Claudius, the fourth of the Roman Emperors, Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, who ruled A.D. 41–54; (b) Claudius Lysias, a tribune at Jerusalem.
gloss: Claudius, the fourth of the Roman Emperors

text: κλαυθμός, weeping.
κλείς, a key.
κλέμμα, a theft.
Κλεόπας, Cleopas, one of the two companions of the risen Jesus from Jerusalem to Emmaus.
κλέος, glory, fame.
κλῆμα, a branch.
Κλήμης (Latin, = Clemens), Clement, a fellow-worker of St. Paul in Rome.
gloss: Clement, a fellow-worker of St. Paul in Rome

text: κληρόω, lit. I choose by lot, I appoint by lot; hence I assign; mid. I assign to myself, choose; pass. I am assigned, I am chosen as God's portion (κλῆρος), Eph. i 11.
gloss: I choose by lot, I appoint by lot

text: κλίβανος, an oven, a furnace.
κλίμα, a small geographical division, district, or territory, a portion of a χώρα (which see).
gloss: a small geographical division, district, or territory

text: κλινάριον, a couch or litter of a sick person.
gloss: a couch or litter of a sick person

text: κλίνη, a couch, a bed, alike a mere mat (e.g. Mt. ix 2, 6), and a more elaborate structure (e.g. Mk. iv 21); possibly a bier in Rev. ii 22.
κλινίδιον, a couch or litter of a sick person.
gloss: a couch or litter of a sick person

text: κλίνω, (A) tr. (a) I rest, recline (even in John xix 30); I bend, incline; (b) (inclino) I cause to give ground, I make to yield, Heb. xi 34; (B) intr. of the day, declines, approaches its end, Lk. ix 12, xxiv 29.
κλισία, properly a dining couch; hence a group of diners.
κλοπή, thieving, theft.
κλύδων, rough water, roughness of water; κ. θαλάσσης a rough sea, James i 6.
κλυδωνίζω, I toss as in a storm at sea.
gloss: I toss as in a storm at sea
note: headword printed κλυδωνίζω; italic t crossbars faint in 'toss' and 'at' (image looks like 'loss', 'al')

text: Κλωπᾶς, Clopas, husband of one Mary, who stood by the cross.
gloss: Clopas, husband of one Mary, who stood by the cross

text: κνήθω, I rub, tickle: κνηθόμενοι τὴν ἀκοήν, with ears itching with eagerness to hear pleasant things, 2 Tim. iv 3.
Κνίδος, Cnidus, a town on the coast of Caria (SW. Asia Minor) near the island of Cos.
gloss: Cnidus, a town on the coast of Caria

text: κοδράντης (Latin, = quadrans), a quadrans, the smallest Roman copper coin, a quarter of an as, the sixteenth part of a sestertius.
gloss: a quadrans, the smallest Roman copper coin

text: κοίμησις, sleeping, followed by constituent gen. τοῦ ὕπνου, which is slumber.
κοινωνικός, willing to share.
κοίτη, (a) a bed, Lk. xi 7; (b) a marriage bed, Heb. xiii 4; κοίτην ἔχειν ἐκ, to conceive seed from, Rom. ix 10: κοῖται plur. repeated (immoral) sexual intercourse, Rom. xiii 13.
κοιτών (cubiculum), bed-chamber: ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ κοιτῶνος (cubicularius), chamberlain.
κόκκινος, crimson, dyed with Kermes (coccum), the female coccus of the Kermes oak.
κόκκος, a grain.
κολάζω, I punish; mid. I cause to be punished.
κολακεία (adulatio), flattery, with a view to advantage or gain.
κόλασις, punishing, punishment, perhaps with the idea of deprivation, 1 John iv 18.
κολαφίζω, I strike with the fist; hence, I maltreat violently.
κολλούριον, eye-salve.
κολλυβιστής (from κόλλυβος, a commission paid on exchange), a money-changer, who changed heathen into Jewish money, for payment into the Temple treasury.
κολοβόω (lit. I maim, mutilate), I cut short, shorten, abbreviate.
Κολοσσαί, Colossae, a town of the Roman province Asia, in the Lycus valley, near Laodicea and Hierapolis.
gloss: Colossae, a town of the Roman province Asia

text: κόλπος, (a) sing. and plur. bosom; (sinus) the overhanging fold of the garment used as a pocket, Lk. vi 38; (b) a bay, gulf, Ac. xxvii 39.
κολυμβάω, (properly I dive; hence) I swim.
κολυμβήθρα (lit. a diving or swimming place), a pool.
κολωνία (Latin, = colonia), a colony, a city settlement of Roman (soldier) citizens; a garrison city.
κομάω, I wear the hair long, I allow the hair to grow long.
gloss: I wear the hair long, I allow the hair to grow long

text: κόμη, hair, long hair.
κομψῶς (colloquial), nicely, finely, bravely.
note: headword printed κομψῶς (Souter's entry for the positive adverb; NT form κομψότερον)

text: κονιάω, I whitewash.
κονιορτός, dust.
κοπάζω, I cease, drop.
κοπετός (planctus), beating of the breast or head in lamentation, lamentation.
gloss: beating of the breast or head in lamentation

text: κοπή (caedes), slaughter.
κοπρία, manure.
κόπριον, manure.
κόραξ, a raven.
κοράσιον (colloquial), a little girl, a young girl; a girl.
gloss: a little girl, a young girl

text: κορβάν (Aramaic), a gift.
κορβανᾶς, the temple treasure.
Κορέ (Hebr.), Korah (Num. xvi 1 ff.).
κορέννυμι, I fill, sate, glut, feed full.
gloss: I fill, sate, glut, feed full

text: Κορίνθιος, Corinthian, of Corinth.
Κόρινθος, Corinth, in NE. Peloponnese, the capital of the Roman province Achaia.
Κορνήλιος, Cornelius, a centurion of the Roman army, stationed at Caesarea (b).
gloss: Cornelius, a centurion of the Roman army

text: κόρος (Hebr.), a (dry) measure, equivalent to ten Attic μέδιμνοι or 120 gallons.
κοσμικός, earthly, worldly (belonging to the present, earthly world as opposed to the heavenly and future).
κόσμιος, orderly, virtuous.
κοσμοκράτωρ, ruler of this world, that is, of the world as asserting its independence of God; used of the angelic or demonic powers controlling the sublunary world, cf. ἀρχή, ἐξουσία, στοιχεῖον.
Κούαρτος, Quartus, a Christian, brother of Erastus the Corinthian. Cf. ἀδελφός.
gloss: Quartus, a Christian, brother of Erastus the Corinthian

text: κούμ (κοῦμι) (Aramaic), arise.
κουστωδία (Latin, = custodia), concr., a guard.
κουφίζω, I lighten.
κόφινος (cophinus), a stiff wicker basket.
κραιπάλη (crapula), surfeiting.
κρανίον, the skull.
κράσπεδον, the fringe, the edge.
κραταιόομαι, I become strong.
κραταιός, strong, powerful.
κράτιστος (egregius), most excellent, an official epithet, used in addressing a Roman of high rank, and in the second century one of equestrian (as distinguished from senatorial) rank.
κραυγάζω, I cry aloud, shout.
κραυγή, (a) a shout, cry, clamour; (b) outcry, clamouring against another, Eph. iv 31.
κρέας (caro), flesh: plur. (carnes) pieces of flesh, kinds of flesh.
κρεμάννυμι (pendo), I hang, I suspend; mid. (pendeo) I am hanging, I hang.
κρημνός, a crag, precipice.
Κρής, a Cretan, an inhabitant of Crete.
gloss: a Cretan, an inhabitant of Crete

text: Κρήσκης (Latin, = Crescens), Crescens, a Christian, coadjutor of St. Paul.
gloss: Crescens, a Christian, coadjutor of St. Paul

text: Κρήτη, Crete: see Κυρήνη.
κριθή, barley.
κρίθινος, made of barley.
κρίνον, a lily growing wild, variously identified with the red anemone, the white lily, the sword lily.
Κρῖσπος, Crispus, ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, converted and baptized by St. Paul.
gloss: Crispus, ruler of the synagogue at Corinth

text: κριτήριον, (a) a law-court, James ii 6; (b) a law-case before an arbiter.
κριτικός, able to judge.
κρούω (pulso), I beat a door with a stick, to gain admittance.
gloss: I beat a door with a stick, to gain admittance

text: κρύπτη (κρυπτή), a hidden place, cf. κρυπτός.
κρυσταλλίζω, I am clear as crystal.
κρύσταλλος, crystal.
κρυφαῖος, hidden, secret: ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ = ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ.
κρυφῆ, in secret, secretly.
note: no iota subscript visible under the η of the headword (printed κρυφῆ?); may be lost in the scan

text: κτάομαι, (a) I acquire, win, get, purchase, buy; (b) I possess, 1 Thess. iv 4.
gloss: I acquire, win, get, purchase, buy

text: κτῆμα, a piece of landed property, a field, Ac. v 1; plur. possessions, property, possibly landed property, property in land in Mk. x 22, Mt. xix 22, as it is in Ac. ii 45.
gloss: a piece of landed property, a field

text: κτῆνος, a beast of burden (generally, a horse or mule), either for riding or for carrying loads on its back, or for yoking to a cart or carriage.
κτήτωρ, a possessor, owner.
κτίσμα, a created thing, a creature, of God.
κτίστης (often of the founder of a city), creator, God.
κυβεία, (lit. playing with dice, gaming, hence) trickery, sleight.
κυβέρνησις (lit. steering, piloting), governing, government, supposed to refer to such duty as was, later at least, performed by any presbyter or by that presbyter who was ἐπίσκοπος.
κυβερνήτης, a steersman, a pilot.
κυκλεύω, I encircle, invest, enclose.
κυκλόθεν, in a circle round, round about.
gloss: in a circle round, round about

text: κυκλόω, I encircle, invest, surround.
κυλισμός, rolling, wallowing.
κυλλός (debilis), maimed.
κῦμα, a wave.
κύμβαλον, a cymbal.
κύμινον (a Semitic word), cummin, a plant used as a spice.
gloss: cummin, a plant used as a spice

text: κυνάριον, a house dog, possibly with a touch of contempt.
Κύπριος, Cypriote, belonging to Cyprus.
Κύπρος, Cyprus.
κύπτω, I stoop.
Κυρηναῖος, belonging to Cyrene.
Κυρήνη, Cyrene, a district W. of Egypt on the Mediterranean coast, forming with Crete a Roman province.
gloss: Cyrene, a district W. of Egypt on the Mediterranean coast

text: Κυρήνιος, Publius Sulpicius Quirinius (ob. A.D. 21), who conducted two censuses of the province Syria, one in 8, 7, or 6 B.C., Lk. ii 2, as plenipotentiary of the Emperor, and another as legatus pro praetore in A.D. 7, Ac. v 37.
